chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: The jumping German club where young fans adored the band
summary: On the Red Richards European tour a huge German club's young crowds, new to this music, kissed and danced with the band, and the manager signed them for a return.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, wrong, yes. So one day you keep hoping maybe a little longer and they will see, say man, this is it! Too many times, oh, well that's one, and in Europe with Red Richards. We were in -- ah, Amsterdam. Amsterdam? Germany? Yeah -- huh?
No, not Holland. No, Germany. Uh, (taps) damn -- dam, it's --

No, no. No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. We had a heck of a thing there, though. It's a big thing. It was jumping, and had two bands in there, and it's a big place, and they're doing -- yeah, yang, yang, yang-yang-yang, yang -- oh man! You know. God doggy!
This was some place in Germany.
Oh, big city. Uh -- my wife's -- the band -- one of the boss's -- his wife, she worked there, so that's where he was from. Anyway, I was -- it'll come to me in a minute.

We were playing there, and where the waitresses had cleared the place, it was so dark you couldn't see what in the heck you were doing. Man! That was the God damndest joint! On the way back I was going back to the dressing room, put my horn down, hang my coat up, or put it down, or something. I passed couples in the corners, in booths, and whatnot, and they were making it! I mean everything was happening! Nobody -- shoot, they paid me no mind.

And when the curtain -- when the lights would go on I never saw so many pretty looking gals and nice looking boys in all my life. They were beautiful. So the other band started, and we started playing, and the kids come up and they say who are you? Where did they come from? This is something new. They'd never -- they had never heard of anything like what -- Oh, and they came up, and they put their arms around
us on the bandstand, they kiss us, and holding, and dancing with us.
So the manager came up. He said will you sign a contract right now? He said I'd like to bring you back in six weeks, so many weeks. And we signed a contract, and the money was fabulous.

Well then, we never heard anything -- you're new! What do you call this? What is this called? And they'd say you know, I played, bang! bang-a-bang! So loud you couldn't hear your ear lobes, and falling out and everything, and we start playing tunes, and -- enh (snap), buts (snap), buts (snap), bits (snap) bah, oh beeble deeble deeble, doo, you know. And they were out there dancing, and they -- you know, best they could, because they didn't know about any what you call it, way you used to dance here.

Lindy Hop. They didn't know nothing about that. I mean once in a while -- once, you'd look, you see a person who has seen or heard of a little of it, and they were -- well watch and see what this guy's doing, and they began to feel it, and they wanted to get with it, and they have to, they find out they have to. And that was it!
